title: FDA to prioritize guidance on AI, surgical robots next year
key_facts: The FDA outlined its A-list and B-list guidance priorities for the 2027 fiscal year: lists of priority final and draft guidance documents, documents it will publish if resources permit, and texts under construction.
The priority lists have seven final guidance documents (one a holdover from last year) and one draft text; the FDA is accepting feedback until 30 Nov.
Finalizing the January 2025 draft guidance on lifecycle management for AI-enabled devices is now a priority; it was only a second-tier goal last year.
New this year: drafting evidence recommendations for generative-AI conversational devices for mental disorders, following an August call for feedback on regulating generative AI.
The FDA aims to finalize guidance on premarket submissions for robotically assisted surgical devices within a year of the draft; feedback on that draft is open until 24 Nov.
Other final-guidance priorities: air-purifying respirators, menstrual product testing and labeling, quality management systems, and the accreditation scheme for conformity assessment.

Holdover from last year: guidance on predetermined change control plans for medical devices is still unfinished; a guidance on validating certain in vitro diagnostics, a priority last year, is not on this year's list.
Second-tier priority: finalizing pulse oximeter guidance (draft from January 2025), responding to concerns about skin pigmentation affecting accuracy.
quote_evidence: The FDA is accepting feedback on its priorities until Nov. 30.
In January 2025, the FDA published the draft version of the guidance on lifecycle management for AI-enabled devices now prioritized for finalization.
The FDA also aims to finalize guidance on premarket submissions of robotically assisted surgical devices in the coming year.
why_it_matters_hint: Device makers and AI developers can see which FDA advice on AI devices and surgical robots is most likely to be finished within a year.
event_date: Not stated in the article; MedTech Dive published it 2 Oct 2026.
notes: One trade outlet reporting the FDA's own list; the FDA document itself was not read. The list is a proposal open for comment. Guidance is the FDA's written advice to device makers (explained for readers, not stated in the article).
